transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-08
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Lopez (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood PM lead), Lena Zhou (AuroraCloud PM), Carlos Ruiz (AuroraCloud Partnerships), Priya Singh (AuroraCloud Platform Engineer), David Park (AuroraCloud Security)

Auto-summary: Quick partner technical sync to map out marketplace listing logistics and technical integration for Redwood's marketplace listing on AuroraCloud. Focus on RA for private deployments, IAM roles needed, data residency and KMS integration, and hands-on POC steps.

Topics discussed:
- Listing checklist and required artifacts (logos, SKUs, pricing model)
- Reference architecture: VPC connectors, private control plane, data flow, KMS/HSM integration
- Joint solution packaging: how Redwood will appear in AuroraCloud marketplace (managed vs bring-your-own)
- Security and compliance: SOC2, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC mapping
- Performance validation: benchmarking plan and SLA targets

Transcript (timestamps are approximate):
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick off, we're excited about the AuroraCloud marketplace listing and wanted to run through integration specifics and the RA for private deployments. Evan and Jordan are here to cover technical and PM questions.
[00:18] Lena (AuroraCloud): Thanks Maya, yep we sent a short pre-read, but the core here is to make sure the listing flow and RA align with our marketplace ops. We have two models — managed listing and marketplace-managed (you know, like a managed offering) and a BYO (bring your own) private package.
[00:35] Evan (Redwood SE): Quick callout: Redwood supports hosted, dedicated and private — for marketplace we usually support both a managed offering (hosted API via Redwood) and a private deployment reference that customers can install in their VPC with a single sign-on flow. We need to align on which one Aurora wants to surface first.
[00:52] Carlos (AuroraCloud): For initial buyers we prefer a managed listing to reduce friction; we can add private as "deployable" option later. That said, we have enterprise customers who'll require VPC-only and dedicated host model.
[01:12] Priya (AuroraCloud): From platform side, we'll need a reference arch doc that shows how the private control plane talks to Aurora's marketplace provisioning, the required IAM roles, and what telemetry/audit logs are sent back.
[01:27] Jordan (Redwood): Makes sense. Evan, can you run through the RA at a high level?
[01:33] Evan (Redwood SE): Sure — high level, we recommend a private control plane in customer's VPC, optional agent/connector to Aurora's marketplace for licensing and billing hooks, KMS integration for keys, and an ingress policy for the model serving nodes. For performance, we usually include guidance on GPU types, instance sizes, and quantization profiles.
[01:52] David (AuroraCloud Security): On the KMS callout — we enforce customer-managed keys for enterprise listings. We'll need to validate the HSM/KMS compatibility and key rotation flows. Also audit logs need to include per-request metadata for billing reconciliation.
[02:10] Maya: Noted. We can surface our KMS integration patterns and sample audit log schema. I'll share a checklist with the marketplace listing fields (logo, description, SKUs, pricing) and a sample IAM policy.
[02:24] Lena: Great. On the billing schema — we need tokens-per-call or per-invoice mappings; can Redwood produce a billing export we can map into our invoicing?
[02:36] Evan: Yes, we have token-level usage exports and per-route cost breakdown — we can give a sample CSV and a mapping doc. There might be slight naming mismatch (we call routes and customers may call them plans) — but it's straightforward.
[02:53] Carlos: Competitors to watch: CloudMart and NovaEdge both have similar marketplace flows; CloudMart has a tighter billing integration with automatic invoices which we like.
[03:06] Maya: Good to know. We'll include a sample integration that mimics your auto-invoice fields.
[03:12] 
[03:30] (deep technical section)
[03:30] Evan: For the RA, the main components we propose:
- Private control plane (optional hosted control plane for managed customers)
- Model serving fleet (dedicated GPU pools) behind Aurora VPC endpoints
- A provisioning webhook that the Aurora marketplace calls to trigger deployment with a minimal stack template (we'll provide Terraform/ARM/CloudFormation variants)
- KMS/HSM integration for model encryption at rest and for signing audit events
- Metrics and logs forwarded to Aurora's telemetry ingestion endpoint with RBAC-limited tokens
[04:12] Priya: The webhook approach works. We do want the stack templates because our ops people prefer IaC-first. Can you include a minimal Terraform example?
[04:22] Evan: Yes, we'll prepare a Terraform starter that provisions the connector and the minimal infra. It will include example RBAC roles.
[04:28] Lena: On the listing UX, we need a one-line description, three bullets of capabilities, pricing model (usage vs subscription), and a security FAQ.
[04:38] Maya: We'll draft that and send over.
[04:42] 
[04:55] (conversation about latency/cost tradeoffs)
[04:55] David (Security): Also, do you have any SOC2/ISO attestation docs? We need those before enterprise customers can purchase.
[05:05] Maya: We are SOC2 Type II certified — I'll attach the cert and the compliance pack. Evan will add notes on audit log retention and access controls.
[05:14] Evan: On audit logs, we can push a per-request event that includes an obfuscated user id, request id, model id, tokens in/out, and status. We can redact content by default; content-level logging is opt-in.
[05:31] Priya: Perfect. For KMS, what's your recommended rotation schedule?
[05:36] Evan: We recommend 90-day rotation for customer-managed keys, and we support automatic re-encryption in our runtime. We'll include the operational playbook.
[05:44] 
[06:00] (discussion on POC and perf targets)
[06:00] Jordan: For the POC we propose a 2-week pilot: set up a reference deployment in a sandbox, run a small benchmark set, and validate billing exports. Target metrics: p99 latency under 300ms for text-gen small models and throughput of X tokens/sec per GPU — we'll define exact numbers in the doc.
[06:20] Lena: That timeline is fine. Who runs the benchmark? Redwood or Aurora?
[06:26] Evan: We'll run the initial perf run in our sandbox and send the scripts; if Aurora wants, we can run the same in your environment to compare.
[06:34] Carlos: We'll need the exact scripts and synthetic workloads. Also any infra costs should be estimated so procurement knows expected spend for POC.
[06:44] Maya: We'll include an estimated cost card for the POC and a sample script repo link (we'll share after call).
[06:52] 
[07:10] (mis-transcription / filler)
[07:10] Speaker 1: uh we also, um, might want like a fallback policy, right, if a customer's infra is down?
[07:16] Evan: ya, Redwood supports smart routing to fallback to hosted variants in cross-region failover — but that requires opt-in from the customer and must be enabled in the marketplace listing as an option.
[07:28] Priya: We need to check legal on cross-region failover for some regulated customers, might be blocked.
[07:35] David: yes, data residency concerns. We should include explicit data flow diagrams and a residency statement in the listing.
[07:42] 
[07:55] (reference links mentioned)
[07:55] Maya: Links I'll send: 1) marketplace listing checklist (Google Doc), 2) sample IAM policies (gist link), 3) Terraform starter repo (GitHub link), 4) sample billing CSV.
[08:07] Lena: Please attach in the follow-up email and in the marketplace portal too.
[08:12] Maya: will do.
[08:20] 
[08:30] (security nuance)
[08:30] David: One nuance — for some customers audit logs need to be stored for seven years. Does Redwood provide long-term archival hooks?
[08:39] Evan: We can export logs to S3-compatible archival storage with lifecycle policies; we'll document retention and archival endpoints.
[08:47] Priya: Also need to know whether Redwood's connectors require outbound internet egress from the customer's VPC or can operate via private endpoints only.
[08:56] Evan: Connector supports private endpoints; by default we prefer VPC endpoints and direct peering. Only the hosted-control-plane managed flow requires optional egress for updates unless the customer opts for an air-gapped package.
[09:10] Maya: We'll capture those two modes in the RA doc — "private endpoints" and "air-gapped install" with the differences called out.
[09:18] 
[09:35] (procurement and timeline)
[09:35] Carlos: On go-to-market timing, AuroraCloud marketplace has a review window of 10 business days for listing assets, plus technical review for RA and security. If we get docs by Jun 10 we can aim for a public listing by end of July.
[09:52] Maya: Sounds good. We'll aim for Jun 10 deliverables.
[09:57] 
[10:10] (closing, recap)
[10:10] Maya: Recap: Redwood to send marketplace checklist, IAM examples, Terraform starter, billing CSV; Redwood to run initial POC perf runs and share scripts; Aurora to grant sandbox access and provide billing schema. Evan will draft RA and Jordan will coordinate PM-level items. Any blockers?
[10:29] Lena: No blockers from our side, just need the docs and sandbox.
[10:33] David: Security will review the RA and attestations. We might ask follow-ups on KMS rotation.
[10:40] Maya: Great — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[10:45] 
[10:50] (after call notes)
[10:50] ACTIONS: Maya to send checklist and compliance pack; Evan to prepare Terraform starter and perf script; Priya to provision sandbox creds.

End of transcript.

Shared artifacts mentioned (links to be shared in follow-up):
- Marketplace listing checklist (doc)
- Sample IAM policies (gist)
- Terraform starter repo (github.com/redwood/auroracloud-terraform-starter)
- Billing export sample (CSV)
- SOC2 attestation (PDF)

Notes on transcription: Some speaker labels are generic (Speaker 1) in a few spots; transcription includes a couple of mis-hearings (e.g., "auto-invoice" transcribed differently). Real follow-up email will include corrected attachments and canonical docs.

Recap & next steps (as discussed):
- Maya to share listing checklist, IAM examples, SOC2 pack by 2027-06-10
- Priya to provide sandbox account and billing schema by 2027-06-14
- Evan to run POC perf tests and share scripts and preliminary numbers by 2027-06-18
- Schedule RA demo week of 2027-06-21 (Jordan to coordinate)
